climbing_route.label: East face to the northeast ridge
climbing_route.notes: From the col, scramble up loose scree and talus on Blackcap's east face to gain the northeast ridge, where the rock transitions to distinctive black hornfels/shale.

climbing_route.label: Northeast ridge to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge, staying on its left/south side as terrain allows, on easy Class 2-3 with some exposure and loose rock near the top. The ridge includes one true knife-edge section with easy-to-moderate exposure, distinct from the otherwise mellow class 2-3 terrain. Camp-to-summit is about 5-6 hours round trip.

wa_booker_mountain_northwest_route.skip_reason: The approach text is entirely the multi-day backpack to Park Creek Pass. The only reference to the climb is one clause - a short day-trip scramble up to the Booker-Buckner col and on to the summit - with no terrain, class, side, or hazards described. There is nothing to re-home.

climbing_route.label: Pumice and talus slopes to the south ridge
climbing_route.notes: From the basin, ascend broad pumice and talus slopes and a low-angle snowfield to gain the south ridge around 7,400 ft; an ice axe, and crampons in early season, are worth carrying.

climbing_route.label: South ridge crest to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge crest through Class 2-3 terrain, stepping to locally 3-4 near a horn/gendarme close to the true summit, on loose, rubbly, slabby schist. Rockfall/loose schist is the main hazard - helmet recommended, especially with parties above or below. The summit crest has several bumps within feet of each other, so take care identifying the true high point.

climbing_route.label: Ridge crest north from Marmot Pass
climbing_route.notes: The summit route leaves the maintained trail at Marmot Pass: pick up the unsigned climbers'/boot path that follows the open ridge crest north from the pass roughly 1 mile and 900-1,000 ft of gain to the southwest (higher) summit. Not an official trail - expect braided boot paths through heather and talus and a few spots where you'll want hands for balance. Route-finding is straightforward in clear weather (stay near the ridge crest), but the braided paths and cliffy drop-offs on the north side make it easy to wander off-line in fog or whiteout. Lingering snow patches on the upper ridge are possible into early summer.

climbing_route.label: Summit boulder
climbing_route.notes: A short, easy scramble onto the large boulder that forms the true high point.

climbing_route.label: South-facing slope/rib system to the east ridge
climbing_route.notes: From camp, leave the trail and climb the open, south-facing slope/rib system directly below Buckskin's summit - a broad old avalanche path. The rib closest to camp carries the least brush and gives the most direct line; an old, badly overgrown boot path toward the east ridge is generally not worth chasing due to extensive deadfall. Ascend scree and heather roughly 2,000-2,800 ft to gain the east ridge around 7,200-7,900 ft. Loose, ball-bearing scree and wet heather are the hazards on this open slope.

climbing_route.label: East ridge crest to the summit
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge crest - narrow and blocky in spots with minor gendarmes - the final few hundred feet to the 8,127 ft summit. No dependable water above the meadows once you leave the trail, aside from early-season snowmelt.

climbing_route.label: Snow ramp to the notch beside Point 5,841
climbing_route.notes: Above roughly 5,400-5,800 ft, pick a line through talus and boulders to avoid the steepest snow; the final ~200 vertical feet below the pass typically holds a firm, sustained snow ramp well into summer, and an ice axe (crampons/microspikes in early season) is required for this section - it is genuine self-arrest terrain. Near the top of the summit-pass snow ramp, watch for a moat-type gap; a short traverse beneath the snow edge may be needed to reach solid rock. Loose talus/scree on the upper slopes.

climbing_route.label: Ridge traverse from the pass to the summit
climbing_route.notes: From the pass, a short class 3-4 ridge traverse leads to the summit.

wa_cathedral_rock_northwest_couloir.skip_reason: The approach text describes only the drive and trail to Cathedral Pass and then around toward the northwest side of the summit block. It says nothing about the couloir or any climbing above that point.

wa_cinderella_peak_scramble.skip_reason: The text stops at the low notch on the ridge between Cinderella and Little Sister, which it calls the jumping-off point for Cinderella's west ridge/north face - the climbing itself is never described. Everything before that is approach, and the text explicitly calls the class 3 rock steps below the glacier toe the crux of the approach.
